text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower but trimmed losses at the close despite a sharp drop in New York raws. The front month May contract ended the day $1.20 lower at $308 per tonne, but was off an intraday low of $307.40 per tonne, despite a slide in New York. Attentions have turned to the upcoming expiry of the March contract in New York. Traders were also watching news on the strike in key Brazilian port of Santos which started on Monday but was put to an end on the evening of the same day. Raw sugar futures in New York closed near the lows pressured by trade and speculative selling, but short covering helped the most active May contract over support seen at 10.85 cents, traders said. May ended down 0.20 cents at 10.90 cents, having ranged from 11.01 to 10.89 cents. Spot March settled 0.25 cents lower at 10.92 cents, while the outer months finished down 0.09 to 0.16 cents. UNITED STATES - The US Department of Agriculture expects US sugar production in 1997/98 (October/September) to rise to 7.480 short tons, raw value, up from the estimated 1996/97 result of 7.290 million tons. While beet sugar output will rise to 4.320 million tons, up from 4 million tons, cane sugar is expected to drop to 3.250 million tons against 3.290 million tons. Imports are forecast to rise to 2.824 million tons, up from 2.734 million tons. Consumption will continue to rise to 9.900 million tons, the USDA said, adding that the 1996/97 estimate still stood at 9.800 million tons. The US stocks to use ratio will climb somewhat to 15.0 per cent, up from 14.6 per cent in 1996/97. The USDA expects raw sugar quotations in New York to average around 11.10 cents/lb in 1997/98, up from 10.50 cents/lb in 1996/97.

RUSSIA - Russia's Agriculture Ministry has targeted the country's 1997 sugar beet output at 22 million tonnes, up from 16.1 million tonnes produced in 1996. However, it has to be emphasized that Russian production forecast at this time of the year are notoriously optimistic. For example in 1996, the Ministry of Agriculture planned to raise sugar beet production to 19.5 million tonnes, but the actual result fell short of this target by 3.4 million tonnes. As the area sown to beet is to rise only marginally to 1.080 million ha in 1997/98 Russian authority will have to rely on significantly higher yields in order to achieve the production target.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 19,562 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 48,853 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 (October/September) up to 659,840 tonnes, down from 1.139 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 663,985 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were France with 484,679 tonnes whites compared to 947,362 tonnes, Germany with 75,735 tonnes against 68,383 tonnes and the Netherlands with 36,746 tonnes compared to 14,446 tonnes. Sugar exports in September 1996 amounted to 35,176 tonnes, slightly up on last year's 32,648 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 up to 989,122 tonnes against 1.566 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 1.337 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were Syria with 145,839 tonnes whites against 130,706 tonnes, Turkey with 109,920 tonnes against 144,004 tonnes and Israel with 97,353 tonnes, up from 84,692 tonnes.

China bought an additional 22,000 tonnes of raw sugar for March shipment after purchasing 14,000 tonnes earlier this month, trade sources recently said. Mitsui and Kerry were suppliers for the sale but no price details were disclosed, it was added. The vessel Solar Glory, charted by Mitsui, was scheduled to arrive at a Thai port on March 4 to load 12,000 tonnes of sugar while Kerry's ship Marina Lauri had arrived in Bangkok on February 23 to pick up 10,000 tonnes of bagged raw sugar. Traders said the purchases were likely to be used for tolling by the Chinese buyers. Iran's state-run Government Trading Corporation (GTC) bought a cargo of white sugar at $314.00 per tonne for shipment in April, London traders recently said. Last week GTC bought 30,000 tonnes of Cuban raws for March/May shipment and 14,000 tonnes of European Union white sugar, again for April. Prices paid were reported to be $269.00 per tonne for the raws and $313.00 per tonne for the whites, although one trader cited a price of $313.50.
